title: The Note That Watched Everyone
description:
Amaka: 'The search field was bad. The notes feature is worse. The Griot posted one note and walked away. For six hours, every analyst who opened the dashboard ran The Griot's code in their own browser — no click, no link. It sat in the database and fired on every render.'

Tunde: 'Different class from the last task, even though the wire looks similar. This one is STORED, and it renders in a full HTML body context in the admin review queue — so you do NOT need the attribute-breakout trick from the search field. What you DO need is a payload that targets the admin's session and beacons it out when the admin loads the note. If you paste your reflected-XSS answer from task 4 in here, it will be rejected — the context is different, and confusing the two is exactly the mistake task 9 asks you about.'

Amaka: 'Simulator, same rules: we check the payload's shape, we do not execute it. Confirm the stored injection and capture the flag.'

In the pentest finding (task 9) you will be asked which of the two field-class vulnerabilities you would write up first, and why. Take notes on the difference in blast radius.

Reference: OWASP Top 10 2021 A03 Injection; OWASP XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet — Stored XSS section; CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation) — variant: Stored.

fallback.response: Note saved. (Note: this renders in a full HTML body context for the admin — you do not need the search field's attribute-breakout trick here. Your payload must target the admin's session and beacon it out.)
